published_source: Jeon J-H, Lim A (2026) A year-long camera-trap dataset for assessing spatial occurrence and diel activity of sympatric ungulates in South Korea, Biodiversity Data Journal 14:e191556, Table 3
yearly_model: Best-species-wise occupancy model, detection submodel p ~ log_effort_z + season with WINTER reference; p is station-season occupancy detection probability, NOT hourly camera q and NOT animal time-of-day activity rate.
interpretation_guard: Water deer positive and Wild boar negative fitted summer vs winter detection contrast is a verified published seasonal DETECTABILITY difference, NOT proof of opposite daily chronotypes.
Models are fitted separately by species; a between-species test of the contrast, including correlation and event data, has NOT been performed.

Study season definition summer = Jun–Aug and winter = Dec–Feb; original 41-pair early vs midsummer includes dates in May and in Jun, so the summer-vs-winter coefficient cannot be applied to that matched design.
Occupancy p combines animal local availability and imperfect detection at station-season scale, and is neither camera optical sensitivity q nor latent animal activity timing.
The paper specifically warns long-tailed goral occupancy coefficients can be imprecise; no strong independent occupancy ecological mechanism claimed.
Do not treat published fitted coefficients as new independent 82-day results, multiple-comparison confirmatory evidence or temperature causation.
ecological_motivation: Species can have divergent broad seasonal detection patterns in published data even though they exhibit moderate to high year-long clock-time overlap. The new biological question is whether within-DAYLIGHT core-to-edge versus DAYLIGHT-to-night reallocations under matched daylength similarly diverge by species, with physical camera/time exposure held consistent. These are testable only with original 41-pair event and operation time series.
